rubrics.justification: Generally consistent with a fair-quality blastocyst and notes loosely organized ICM/TE, but it overstates certainty about cavity/peripheral definition and includes a questionable discussion of Gardner stage terminology.
Integrates age, ovarian reserve, BMI, endometrium, prior IVF outcomes, male factor, and lifestyle well, though some links (e.g., stress impact, sperm DNA concerns) are somewhat speculative.
Overall logical and internally consistent, with prognosis appropriately tempered by prior failures; minor inconsistency in calling the embryo both good-quality and only fair-to-good/transferable.

Recommendations are largely evidence-based: single embryo transfer, avoid unproven add-ons, consider uterine review and possible PGT-A discussion after failures. Minor issue is the inaccurate statement about strict Gardner expansion staging.
Provides practical next steps for transfer and contingency planning, including luteal support adherence, review of prior cycle details, sperm DNA testing discussion, and uterine assessment if needed.
